notes.s: A debut single that asks a Korean teenager what he wants, then refuses the answer.
notes.t: The group's debut single from June 2013, school uniforms and baggy everything. Its target is specific: the Korean exam track, the compulsory evening study block, the civil-service job a parent names as a dream. Critics at the time heard borrowed American posturing and the group spent years outrunning that reading, but the social argument underneath is the one they kept coming back to in 뱁새 and 고민보다 Go. The closing English line, addressed to youngsters without dreams, is the thesis stated plainly.
k: 얌마 is a flattened 이놈아 by way of 야 임마, the way you shout at a kid or a younger friend, and aiming it at anyone older starts a fight. 뭐니 and 그거니 use -니, a question ending adults point downward at children. So the hook is pitched as a teacher or parent interrogating a student, which is the voice the song mimics and then turns back on them.

야자 is 야간자율학습, the evening study block Korean high schoolers sit at school until ten or later, officially self-directed and attended under compulsion. 독서실, the paid study room in line 11, is the matching alibi you give a parent on the way out. 돌직구 is a stone fastball, slang for saying a thing straight with no cushioning, and the line throws one at the institution.

장래희망 is the phrase printed on a school form where a child writes what they want to become. 공무원, civil servant, is the answer parents of this era wanted, because the entrance exam is impartial and the job never evaporates. Treating it as a dream rather than a job is what the song is attacking, and the charge is in the line before: 틀에 박힌 꿈, a dream stamped out of a mould.

주어 is the grammatical subject, the word that performs the verb. Telling someone to become the subject of their own life puts a Korean classroom term to work, because for the whole song the listener has been the object, 억압만 받던, only ever on the receiving end of pressure. The -아 보다 ending softens the order into give it a try.

vocab.note: It takes 꿈 as its object and nothing else does: 꿈을 꾸다
Lays contempt on a quantity, so 겨우 그거 is that is all?
Interchangeable with 겨우 in this use
Casual for 잊다; the literal sense is to peel and eat, which is why it covers polishing off a snack
A rented desk in a silent room, booked by the month by students and exam takers
유리멘탈 in line 18, glass mental, is the home-made English for the same idea
담아둬 here is pack it away and leave it there

vocab.en: grow up, come to one's senses
vocab.note: 철 is discernment, and 철없다 is what you call a grown adult behaving like a child
틀에 박히다 is to be stuck in a mould, hence stereotyped or rigid
주입식 교육 is the standard phrase for rote, pour-it-in schooling
